newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pan Pacific head resigns, buys media unit.
newsitem.headline: Pan Pacific head resigns, buys media unit.

text.p: Diversified publishing firm Pan Pacific Public Co Ltd said on Friday its managing director, Chong Huai Seng, had resigned with effect from April 10.
Chong had been replaced by Ong Khim Kiat, a substantial shareholder in the company, Pan Pacific said in a statement.
Chong had sold his 10.46 million shares in Pan Pacific, or 18.9 percent of the company, to Ong at Singapore $0.88 per share, it said.
That gave Ong 13.26 million shares, or approximately 24 percent of the company, it said.
Pan Pacific said Chong had agreed to buy Pan Pacific's 33 percent stake in the share capital of Panpac Media Pte Ltd and S$1.25 million worth of the unit's convertible loan stock.

The total consideration in cash payable by Chong for Panpac Media's shares and convertible loan stock was S$5.6 million, comprising S$4.35 million for the shares and S$1.25 for the convertible loan stock.

"In the event the sale is completed, the company will make an extraordiary gain of S$2.95 million for the financial year ending March 31, 1998," it said. "This gain will result in an increase in the net tangible assets backing per share of the company on a consolidated basis of S$0.05."
The Pan Pacific statement did not say if Chong's resignation was related to the failure of the company's associate firm Channel KTV, which was announced in the same statement.
Channel KTV's demise resulted in an extraordinary write-off for Pan Pacific of S$9.5 million.
